title: Fast-path ALU with selective M arithmetic
motivation:

also part of the same wide result mux. CoreMark is dominated by ordinary
integer, address-generation, compare, and control operations, so this
unconditional arithmetic fanout is a likely Fmax limiter and consumes LUTs
without improving its iteration rate.

title: Registered elastic fetch boundary
motivation:
The current IF/ID path is combinational from io_imemData through instruction
decode and the register-file read ports into the ID/EX register. That makes
the external instruction bus, decode fanout, and operand routing share one
long timing path, even though the pipeline already has valid/stall control.
The prior prefetch FIFO was too much front-end state; this targets only the
timing boundary and uses a single elastic entry.

title: Metadata-free trained loop target predictor
motivation:
CoreMark repeatedly executes conditional loop branches, but the five-stage
core waits for EX to resolve each taken branch and flushes the younger
fetch/decode work. Earlier BTBs and early branch resolvers lost Fmax because
they decoded branches in IF or carried prediction metadata through the
common pipeline. The closest prior result was a one-entry exact-PC target
table, so reducing its sideband and limiting it to trained conditional loops
is the most promising remaining predictor direction.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a one-entry full-PC last-target predictor shared by IF and EX. Train it
only from resolved conditional branches: use a two-bit saturating confidence
counter, record the resolved taken target after a taken branch, and replace
or decay the entry on other outcomes. IF consults only the current fetch PC;
a high-confidence exact-PC hit selects the already-registered target, so no
B-immediate decode, target adder, BTB indexing, or prediction token is added
to the instruction bundles. EX re-looks up the exact PC and suppresses its
normal redirect only when the live entry still agrees with the resolved
next-PC; otherwise it performs the existing redirect and flush. Do not
predict JAL/JALR or misaligned targets. This should remove steady-state
backward-loop redirects while keeping cold branches, aliases, table
replacement, not-taken exits, bus stalls, and RVFI pc_wdata on the precise
fallback path.
